title: HPE patches eight max severity RCE and auth bypass AOS flaws
description: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) released security updates addressing 72 vulnerabilities in ArubaOS, including eight maximum-severity flaws involving authentication bypass and remote code execution (RCE). These critical vulnerabilities affect multiple versions of AOS-8 and AOS-10 and can be exploited remotely without privileges or user interaction. HPE strongly urges customers to apply patches promptly and recommends restricting access to management interfaces to reduce exploitation risk. No public exploit code or active exploitation has been reported as of the advisory date.
aiSummary: HPE patched 72 vulnerabilities in ArubaOS, with eight rated maximum severity due to authentication bypass and remote code execution risks. The affected software versions include multiple releases of AOS-8 and AOS-10. The vulnerabilities allow remote attackers to execute code or bypass authentication without privileges or user interaction. HPE advises immediate patching and recommends network segmentation and firewall controls for management interfaces. No proof-of-concept exploits or in-the-wild attacks are currently known.
aiImpact: Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow remote attackers to bypass authentication mechanisms and execute arbitrary code on affected ArubaOS devices. This could compromise enterprise wireless infrastructure components such as mobility conductors, access points, controllers, and gateways. The vulnerabilities pose a significant risk due to their maximum severity rating and ease of exploitation without user interaction. However, no active exploitation has been reported to date.
